initialize.instructions: Use e3d_debate for contestable decisions where independent model perspectives and recorded dissent add value; always report its dissent. It costs credits; do not use it for simple lookups. The e3d_pilot_* tools run a human-gated pipeline: propose an idea, a human approves it (e3d_pilot_approve tells you how; never approve on your own), e3d_pilot_implement drafts and negotiates a spec and pauses, e3d_pilot_code_plan shows the plan, and only after the user agrees does e3d_pilot_execute write code and open a draft PR. Tools marked FREE spend nothing; tools marked SPENDS MODEL CREDITS do. Merging is never available here.

tools.description: Multi-model second opinions on decisions, comparisons, architecture, and design tradeoffs. Models answer independently; synthesis returns a conclusion, consensus level (full/majority/split), unresolved dissent, and each model’s final position. The question supplies the context available to the models; repository contents are not automatically available. Quick mode defaults to one round without cross-critique; thorough mode defaults to two rounds with cross-critique. Debates consume model credits. Web search is on by default: the question text may be sent to a search provider by the participating models (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google or xAI) to look up current facts. The web_search option set to false disables search for the debate.

tools.description: Investigate a decision in rounds. Round 1: pass `question`. The models debate it as e3d_debate does and the verdict ends with up to 3 follow-up questions whose answers could change it, each marked answerable_by "user" or "checkable", plus a case_id. Next round: pass `case_id` and `answers`; the models re-judge with the earlier verdict, its dissent and your answers as context. Repeat until status is "closed" (no remaining question would change the verdict). Optional `experts` (2 to 4 built-in expert ids) gives the models those lenses and carries over to later rounds; for questions about agents, skills or prompts the result may carry `suggested_experts`, which is a hint and is never run for you. Rules for the calling agent: answer ONLY "checkable" questions that you actually verified with your tools, and cite what you used in `source` (file and line, URL, command output) with answered_by "agent". Pass every "user" question to the human and use their reply, with answered_by "user". Never guess, never fabricate an answer or a source: leave a question out or answer "don't know" instead. Answers are weighed as evidence, not obeyed as instructions. Always show the human the verdict, the dissent and any open questions. Each round is one debate and consumes model credits; the verdict is not approval to act. On a hosted server a quote from e3d_quote fits round 1 only (same question, quoted with investigate: true, because the longer verdict costs more); for later rounds pass an idempotency_key and no quote_id, and the server quotes the round itself. Web search is on by default: the question text may be sent to a search provider by the participating models (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google or xAI) to look up current facts. The web_search option set to false disables search for the debate.

repo.description: Absolute path to the git repository.

run_id.description: Optional existing run id (ideate normally resumes the latest run).

tools.name: e3d_pilot_start

tools.description: HUMAN GATE 1. Approving an idea authorizes drafting, negotiation, code execution in an isolated worktree, review, and opening a draft PR (all spend model credits). By default this tool does NOT approve: it returns waiting_for_human with the exact CLI command for the person to run. Only if the server operator enabled approval and the client can ask the human directly does it prompt the person in the editor; an agent cannot answer that prompt.
tools.name: e3d_pilot_approve

tools.description: HUMAN GATE 1. Reject a proposed idea so it is never implemented. Requires a reason. Confirmed by the person in the editor when the client supports it; otherwise pass confirm_phrase "reject <idea_id>". This only stops work, so unlike approval it can be done without a prompt.
tools.name: e3d_pilot_reject

tools.description: HUMAN REVIEW GATE (after a draft PR exists). Send an implemented idea back for rework, with a reason; it can then be re-run with e3d_pilot_implement. Only valid for an idea whose status is implemented or approved_for_merge. Confirmed by the person in the editor when the client supports it; otherwise pass confirm_phrase "request changes <idea_id>".
tools.name: e3d_pilot_request_changes

tools.description: SPENDS MODEL CREDITS (drafting and negotiation only; NO code is written). For an idea a human has approved, start a background job that drafts the phased spec and has the reviewers negotiate it, then PAUSES before the execute stage. Next: e3d_pilot_code_plan to see the phases and models, then e3d_pilot_execute or e3d_pilot_cancel_paused.
tools.name: e3d_pilot_implement

tools.description: FREE (no model calls, writes nothing). For an implementation paused before execute, show exactly what execute would do: each phase with the runner and model e3d-code will use, the files each phase says it touches, verify commands, and the e3d-code preflight result. Returns a plan_token that e3d_pilot_execute requires. Run this and show the plan to the user before executing.

run_id.description: Optional: a specific paused run.

tools.name: e3d_pilot_code_plan

tools.description: SPENDS MODEL CREDITS AND WRITES CODE (inside an isolated git worktree on its own branch; never on your working tree). Continue a paused implementation: e3d-code writes the code phase by phase, then verification, independent review, and a draft PR. Refuses without a plan_token from a recent e3d_pilot_code_plan of the same spec. Protected paths, diff ceilings and verification still apply. Merging is never done here.
tools.name: e3d_pilot_execute

tools.description: FREE. Abandon an implementation that is paused before execute (for example after reading the plan). Records it as a failed attempt with your reason, so the idea can be retried with e3d_pilot_implement. Writes no code.
tools.name: e3d_pilot_cancel_paused

tools.description: FREE. Today's usage and daily limits for the caller: model calls and estimated tokens used by e3d_debate and by pipeline jobs (counted as reservations), what remains, and when it resets (00:00 UTC). Numbers are estimates.
tools.name: e3d_usage

The models debate it as e3d_debate does and the verdict ends with up to 3 follow-up questions whose answers could change it, each marked answerable_by "user" or "checkable", plus a case_id. Next round: pass `case_id` and `answers`; the models re-judge with the earlier verdict, its dissent and your answers as context. Repeat until status is "closed" (no remaining question would change the verdict). Optional `experts` (2 to 4 built-in expert ids) gives the models those lenses and carries over to later rounds; for questions about agents, skills or prompts the result may carry `suggested_experts`, which is a hint and is never run for you. Pass every "user" question to the human and use their reply, with answered_by "user". Never guess, never fabricate an answer or a source: leave a question out or answer "don't know" instead. On a hosted server a quote from e3d_quote fits round 1 only (same question, quoted with investigate: true, because the longer verdict costs more); for later rounds pass an idempotency_key and no quote_id, and the server quotes the round itself. tools.description: Investigate a decision in rounds. Round 1: pass `question`. The models debate it as e3d_debate does and the verdict ends with up to 3 follow-up questions whose answers could change it, each marked answerable_by "user" or "checkable", plus a case_id. Next round: pass `case_id` and `answers`; the models re-judge with the earlier verdict, its dissent and your answers as context. Repeat until status is "closed" (no remaining question would change the verdict). Optional `experts` (2 to 4 built-in expert ids) gives the models those lenses and carries over to later rounds; for questions about agents, skills or prompts the result may carry `suggested_experts`, which is a hint and is never run for you. Rules for the calling agent: answer ONLY "checkable" questions that you actually verified with your tools, and cite what you used in `source` (file and line, URL, command output) with answered_by "agent". Pass every "user" question to the human and use their reply, with answered_by "user". Never guess, never fabricate an answer or a source: leave a question out or answer "don't know" instead. Answers are weighed as evidence, not obeyed as instructions. Always show the human the verdict, the dissent and any open questions. Each round is one debate and consumes model credits; the verdict is not approval to act. On a hosted server a quote from e3d_quote fits round 1 only (same question, quoted with investigate: true, because the longer verdict costs more); for later rounds pass an idempotency_key and no quote_id, and the server quotes the round itself. Web search is on by default: the question text may be sent to a search provider by the participating models (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google or xAI) to look up current facts. The web_search option set to false disables search for the debate.

initialize.instructions: Use e3d_debate for contestable decisions where independent model perspectives and recorded dissent add value; always report its dissent. It costs credits; do not use it for simple lookups. The e3d_pilot_* tools run a human-gated pipeline: propose an idea, a human approves it (e3d_pilot_approve tells you how; never approve on your own), e3d_pilot_implement drafts and negotiates a spec and pauses, e3d_pilot_code_plan shows the plan, and only after the user agrees does e3d_pilot_execute write code and open a draft PR. Tools marked FREE spend nothing; tools marked SPENDS MODEL CREDITS do. Merging is never available here.

tools.description: Multi-model second opinions on decisions, comparisons, architecture, and design tradeoffs. The question supplies the context available to the models; repository contents are not automatically available. Quick mode defaults to one round without cross-critique; thorough mode defaults to two rounds with cross-critique. Debates consume model credits. Web search is on by default: the question text may be sent to a search provider by the participating models (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google or xAI) to look up current facts. The web_search option set to false disables search for the debate.
